Raises resistance by slowing electrons.
Lowers resistance by reducing lattice vibrations.
Makes resistance negative.

questions.explanation: Lower temperature reduces phonon scattering, lowering resistance. Superconductivity is an extreme case.

questions.topic: Capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor
questions.stem: Capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor depends on:

options.text: Current through the capacitor.
Voltage applied across plates.
Charge stored on plates.
Plate area, gap, and dielectric.

questions.explanation: C = kappa epsilon0 A/d depends on geometry and dielectric, not on voltage, charge, or current.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Energy of a charged isolated capacitor
questions.stem: An isolated capacitor C=4.0 microF holds 8.0 microC; find stored energy in microjoules.
questions.explanation: U = Q^2/(2C) = (8e-6)^2/(8e-6) = 8e-6 J = 8 microJ. Use isolated formula.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Energy stored in a capacitor
questions.stem: Two 6.0 microF capacitors in series in the coach's plan; find equivalent capacitance in microF.
questions.explanation: 1/C_eq = 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3, so C_eq = 3 microF. Series capacitances combine reciprocally.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Resistance from resistivity, length and cross-section
questions.stem: A student computes resistance as rho A / L; find the error.

options.text: The formula is correct as written.
The formula should be rho L / A, not rho A / L.
Resistivity should be replaced by conductivity.
Length and area should be swapped in meaning.

questions.explanation: Resistance is resistivity times length divided by area. The student inverted length and area.
